item.title: Parsons’ return imminent but doesn’t solve Packers’ biggest problem
item.description: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 29: Micah Parsons #1 of the Green Bay Packers looks on prior to the game against the Carolina Panthers of the game at Lambeau Field on October 29, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images For all of the Green Bay Packers’ issues through ten games of the 2026 season, getting to the quarterback generally hasn’t been one of them. The Packers’ defense ranks fourth in the NFL in sacks this year, with pressure helping the team rank second in interceptions and fifth in overall passer rating against. Now the cavalry appears set to arrive. Micah Parsons is on his way back, seemingly with the intent of playing next Wednesday against the Los Angeles Rams, and his presence will only further bolster the team’s ability to get after the quarterback. It remains to be seen how he will be deployed — expect a light workload for the next few games, perhaps with him only playing on passing downs — but his return should provide an emotional lift as well as a physical one for a defense that’s already playing well. As that last phrase suggests, though, the defense isn’t really the Packers’ problem right now. That is of course the offensive line, where some recent front office decisions have helped set the table for a catastrophic season up front. One can’t help wondering if this team would be functioning better had Elgton Jenkins been kept around for one more year; had the team not invested so much money in Aaron Banks; had Anthony Belton — wait, the front office drafted him as a guard and he’s been thrust in at tackle by circumstance and the coaching staff, so that one probably isn’t on the front office. And then there is that coaching staff. From a poor overall offensive game plan last week against Minnesota to players seemingly having no idea what they’re doing on a play-to-play basis, the offensive coaches should have spent their few off days in a shortened bye week doing some serious self-evaluation. So, while Parsons’ return is an exciting storyline for the Packers, it almost feels like we’re adding the whipped cream on top of an excellent pumpkin pie while smoke is billowing out of the oven as the turkey burns. So let’s get that main course under control, yeah? Packers cut Pierre Strong to clear roster spot for Micah Parsons’ imminent return | Packersnews.com ($) Strong’s release is all but assuredly a move to open a roster spot for #1, and we should probably expect Strong to return to the practice squad if he clears waivers. item.title: ATP increases player compensation to $350m
item.description: The season-ending ATP Finals is currently taking place in Turin [Getty Images] The men's ATP Tour is promising its players rewards of at least $350m in 2028 - but the board has delayed a decision on hotly disputed changes to doubles until next month. The bonus pool will increase from the current $21.5m to $50m in 2028, with payments offered to players ranked in the world's top 30 at the start of each Masters 1000 event. The world number one will receive the highest bonus of $2m for each of the Masters events they play. A total of $25m will also be shared out between the world's top 250 players at the end of each season, with the goal for everyone to receive $100,000. That would make a significant difference to the finances of lower-ranked players. Players will also no longer be penalised so directly for missing tournaments through injury. World number two Jannik Sinner, for example, won five Masters events in a row between March and May, but may only qualify for 25% of his bonus as he has not been able to play since Wimbledon. Doubles changes 'a sensitive issue' Proposed changes to the doubles - which includes halving draw sizes and reducing the percentage of prize money from 20% to 10% - have received fierce opposition from the players. In October, more than 150 men's doubles players wrote an open letter to the ATP Tour urging them to reconsider "drastic" changes to the format. Chairman Andrea Gaudenzi told BBC Sport the governing body of men's tennis needed "a bit more time to reach consensus". "It is a sensitive issue," he said. "I hope we find the right balance between the players' and the tournaments' demands, and I truly hope we reach a compromise." The proposals will now be voted on next month. Doubles players have said the changes would make it "effectively impossible" for anyone outside the top 30 to make a living from the sport. There may be a hint of compromise in the air, but Gaudenzi still believes at least some of the doubles money needs to be redirected towards singles players. "It's impossible to make everyone happy. It's something we do not take lightly, but we also cannot ignore the fans and the broadcasters - [just] like any entertainment business," he said. "Whether you are a musician or an actor, it needs to be rewarded as a function of the entertainment you provide to the fans." Gaudenzi told Britain's Henry Patten, who was unhappy he and CEO Eno Polo were not present when Patten and Harri Heliovaara received the year-end number one trophy, that he had no intention of undermining their achievement. "I understand his disappointment and he's obviously also driven by what we are discussing, and I do understand it's quite emotional their side," Gaudenzi added. "But I was here in the hotel together with Eno - we were actually fighting and negotiating twelve hours a day to get this deal done - so we were really in the trenches all day long." item.title: 'I'll tell more' - Thomas Frank teases truth behind Tottenham sacking as he prepares for Crystal Palace rescue mission
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur v Newcastle United - Premier League - Getty Images Sport Thomas Frank has officially been unveiled as the new Crystal Palace manager, and the Dane wasted no time in addressing his complicated history with former employers Tottenham. As he prepares to lead the struggling Eagles out of the Premier League relegation zone, Frank suggested there is a deeper story behind his short-lived tenure in North London. Frank takes Palace reins after turbulent Spurs spell Crystal Palace appointed the 53-year-old Dane on Monday on a contract until June 2029, replacing Pierre Sage. Thursday afternoon's unveiling marked Frank's first managerial role since Tottenham sacked him earlier this year after under eight months in charge. Before his troubled north London stint, Frank established Brentford in the Premier League and earned a Manager of the Year nomination. Following his Spurs dismissal, he travelled across Japan, Australia, and Denmark before taking over the Eagles. Dane promises future clarity on Tottenham departure Expecting questions about his former club, Frank admitted: "I know today is a lot about me". While keeping the focus on Palace, he suggested the full story of his Spurs exit will eventually surface. "It’s something I’ve… maybe one day I’ll tell a little bit more about it," Frank said. "I understand why it’s also interesting. I think it’s more about Palace in general today. What can I say? I always said the day I got sacked, I’ll have time to travel, so I think I was relatively quick over it." He added: "But of course you want success, and I’m competitive, so I think that answer probably demands a little bit more time, which I am happy to do one day." Infamous Arsenal cup gaffe still baffles new Eagles boss Frank's Spurs spell unravelled in January when he was pictured drinking from an Arsenal coffee cup ahead of a 3-2 defeat to Bournemouth. For fans already disillusioned with his style of play, the blunder was the final straw, and a five-match winless league run sealed his sacking a month later. Asked if he might accidentally use a cup belonging to Palace's fierce rivals Brighton, Frank smiled. "I hope not," he replied, adding: "I still think it’s a fantastic story." He remains baffled by the backlash to the honest mistake: "I know, and I still don’t understand, how anyone can think that I will drink from a cup from an opponent’s team, that their supporters don’t like, on purpose. Come on. But what a story, huh, to discuss?" Relegation battle and Europa League test await Frank faces an immediate test in lifting Crystal Palace off the bottom of the Premier League table, starting with Saturday's trip to Coventry. Arresting their domestic slump quickly is vital to sparking a survival push. He must also balance European duties, with Palace hosting Real Sociedad in the Europa League next Thursday. Managing energy levels across both fronts will be crucial as the Dane bids to restore his Premier League credentials.

item.title: Sophie Cunningham challenges her male haters to 3-point contest
item.description: Photo by Nick Wosika/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images WNBA star Sophie Cunningham has had enough of armchair critics, and she’s ready to settle things on the court. Sophie Cunningham’s challenge goes straight at one of the tiredest takes in basketball, the idea that any decent guy from the local rec league could hold his own against a WNBA pro. Even with women’s basketball bigger than ever, female players still get hit with the same skepticism about their game every time they log online. The funny thing is, whenever someone actually steps onto the court to test it, reality hits fast. Fans saw Sparks guard Rae Burrell cruise past streamer N3on in a one-on-one, a quick reminder that pro-level talent is on a completely different planet than couch-cushion confidence. Sophie Cunningham challenges men to a three-point contest Speaking on her podcast , Sophie Cunningham finally had enough of guys talking trash about women’s sports from the couch, and decided to call their bluff. She said: “Dude, I think I’ve said enough about where my stance is on this when it comes to boys and girls, I’ll say. But when it comes to regular Joes—what kills me, and even the guys know this—the people talking bad on us women professional athletes, it doesn’t matter the sport, it’s all these men who are laying on the couch, probably eating potato chips. It used to drive me crazy, but now I’m just like, I feel bad for you guys because I don’t know—why are you guys coming after us? “So, what I’m going to say is I think I want to do a challenge here to our listeners, or if you don’t listen, maybe this clip will get out there. I want to find some average Joes—like in the YMCA league and the rec league—who think that they can outshoot me, and have a three-point competition because I’m going to smack that a** every single day of the week. So, I’m challenging all these little people behind the screen who think they can beat me. You won’t.” Honestly, it would be must-see TV. Watching a guy from the local rec league try to keep up with a WNBA player would settle the debate and provide great entertainment, especially considering Cunningham actually shot a higher three-point percentage than Steph Curry this past season. Good luck to whoever volunteers. item.title: Blues fan snubs Homes Under the Hammer over Villa's Dion Dublin
item.description: Birmingham City supporter George Pollock, pictured with his wife Catherine, turned down the chance of being on the show [George Pollock] A Birmingham City fan has revealed why he refused to appear on Homes Under the Hammer after discovering the presenter was former Aston Villa striker Dion Dublin. George Pollock and his wife Catherine, from Castle Bromwich, were approached by the BBC daytime show's production team after buying a property at auction to renovate and sell on. While Catherine jumped at the chance to feature on the programme, George was rather less enthusiastic, and finding out who would be presenting the episode did not help. George said: "Catherine turned around and told me, 'It's going to be Dion Dublin.' I was like, 'Oh, you do it!' "I didn't really want to spend a day with a Villa player." Dublin played for Aston Villa between 1998 and 2002, scoring 48 goals in 65 appearances, becoming a popular figure at Villa Park. Catherine, meanwhile, was happy to go ahead with the filming, but she knew her husband would not feel the same after learning who would be presenting their episode. "If he says he doesn't want to do something, he's probably not going to. Especially when it comes to football," joked Catherine, who appeared in the episode alone. When the reason for her husband's absence was revealed on the show, Dublin could not help but laugh and commend the fan. "I love that he's a proper Blues fan, good lad," he said. Dion Dublin played for Aston Villa between 1998 and 2002 [BBC/lion production] The couple had bought the property with plans to do it up before selling it but had not initially expected their renovation project to end up on television. The Homes Under the Hammer team regularly keep an eye on property auctions to find potential homes and buyers to feature on the show. For lifelong Blues supporter George, however, there was one problem with the whole arrangement. He explained that his love of Birmingham City was passed down by his father, making the prospect of spending a day with a former Villa player a step too far. He joked: "When you're raised on it, you can't get rid of it and I'm sure the other side would have done the exact same. "I've heard he was a good sport about it," added George, who never did meet Dublin. The story has since sparked plenty of amusement on social media, with football fans enjoying the light-hearted rivalry. George said: "It's petty but it's fun petty." Mauricio Pochettino's very first day on the job at Manchester United has already been met with a crisis as the club was victim of an embarrassing security breach. The Argentine has only just arrived as new United manager, flying into Manchester on Wednesday morning, having departed straight after his final game with the U.S. national team on Tuesday night. He has only a few days to prepare for his debut as Red Devils' boss, a difficult challenge on the road at Anfield. The individual flew a drone high above the training ground and filmed Pochettino running drills and giving tactical instructions to his new Red Devils squad, an event which is usually highly confidential and secretive as to avoid giving opponents clear insight into how teams will line up or approach matches. item.title: Urban Meyer Shoots Down Desmond Howard’s Heisman Thoughts
item.description: Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) celebrates after scoring a touchdown in the second half of the NCAA football game at Ohio Stadium on Nov. 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. Former Ohio State coach Urban Meyer has publicly rejected 1991 Heisman winner Desmond Howard’s doubts about Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith’s candidacy for the trophy. Howard, speaking on ESPN’s First Take on Nov. 13, questioned whether Smith has delivered in marquee games. “In the last two years, give me one game where Jeremiah Smith … was the difference in a big game,” Howard said. “As much as he puts up these magnificent numbers and these one-handed catches, I need moments against the top competition that make me say ‘he was the guy.'” Meyer, appearing on The Triple Option podcast, was direct in response . “He’s gonna win [the Heisman]. Are we kidding?” he said. Acknowledging that Ohio State’s losses to USC (30-18) and Oregon (41-28) left a “bad taste,” Meyer defended the junior receiver’s effort: “Did he do everything possible to go win those games? Yeah, he did. The fact that Desmond Howard said, ‘I don’t see him making plays in the big games’… I don’t agree with that.” Smith caught 10 passes for 83 yards and a touchdown at USC and seven for 133 yards and a score against Oregon. Meyer added that the award will partly reflect Smith’s body of work, including a national title as a freshman, while insisting the trophy still goes to the best player. Ohio State sits at 7-3 as Smith continues to push his case to become only the sixth wide receiver to win the Heisman.

item.description: Victor Wembanyama of the San Antonio Spurs brings the ball upcourt during a game gainst the Utah Jazz at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City on Sunday. Photograph: Chris Gardner/Getty Images It wouldn’t be exactly right to say Victor Wembanyama didn’t miss a beat after a disastrous NBA finals in June that left him and his San Antonio Spurs defeated, memed and embarrassed. In the Spurs’ first game this season, against an Oklahoma City Thunder team since decimated by injuries, Wemby went an appalling 1-for-13 from the field. Ten of his 12 points came via free throws. After getting blocked by Aday Mara, the Thunder’s 7ft 3in offseason pickup clearly designed to counter the even more towering Wembanyama, he leaned over his knees and muttered furiously to himself as if trying to exorcise an intrusive thought. It brought to mind an image from the NBA finals a few months earlier: Wemby on the floor after being fouled by the Knicks’ Mitchell Robinson, crowing, “I’m in your head!” The Spurs went on to blow a 29-point lead , lose the game and the finals. Now Wemby seemed too preoccupied with the issues within his own dome to worry about wreaking havoc in anybody else’s. Related: Steph Curry’s defense of Ayesha exposes the ugly double standards of sports’ manosphere | Andrew Lawrence Game two saw Wembanyama elect to lay the ball up instead of dunking it in the dying seconds of a close tilt with the Houston Rockets, which the springy Amen Thompson blocked spectacularly . Not a great start, and in a league whose narratives calcify long before sample sizes reach an adequate scale, it allowed for whispers that the Spurs were in trouble. But you could say Wembanyama has not missed a beat since then . After beginning the season 0-2, the Spurs are now 13-3, with 12 of those wins coming in a row before a loss to the Detroit Pistons on Tuesday. San Antonio’s basketball hasn’t been as seamless as those numbers suggest – the starting lineup includes three guards, leaving the offense a bit clunky and wanting for three-point shooting. It also includes Wembanyama, which papers over pretty much every possible problem. Unofficially crowned the best player in the world during last season’s playoffs , Wembanyama has since distanced his closest challengers for that honor. item.title: Tonda Eckert signs Southampton contract extension after ‘Spygate’ scandal
item.description: Tonda Eckert has signed a contract extension at Southampton after surviving the storm of the ‘Spygate’ scandal . Eckert found himself under immense scrutiny after Southampton were caught spying on their Championship play-off semi-final opponents Middlesbrough last season. An investigation found Saints had also spied on two other teams that seasons and the club were subsequently kicked out of the Championship play-off final and docked four points at the start of the season season, admitting to three breaches of EFL regulations. Eckert accepted responsibility as Southampton opted to stand by their manager despite the controversy, and he was later given a six-week suspended ban - keeping him on the touchline barring any further offences. And despite the hindrance of a points deduction, Southampton have started the season in fine form under Eckert, with the club five points off top spot. The German has now been rewarded with a contract extension that will keep him at the club until 2029. Eckert said: "We've had some conversations that started a couple of weeks ago, and the goal was always clear: to show the same commitment that we have had for the last 12 months. I'm very happy that we have come to the point that we can make it official now. "There is a lot that has happened in the last 12 months, but the commitment from the club, from Dragan, Johannes and Phil, and the supporters, means everything to me. I am very grateful for that. We have started a journey that is not even halfway through - there is a lot more to come." Saints are unbeaten in their last 17 home matches, with Eckert only experiencing one defeat at St Mary’s during his tenure. "I think it's a great commitment from both sides; from the club to Tonda, and from Tonda to the club. I'm very happy that we have achieved this agreement before the end of the international window, allowing us to go into the busy schedule that is ahead of us with clarity,” sporting director Johannes Spors said. "Tonda is very talented and very precise with a great analytical brain, but also has the personality and authority that you need, even at a young age. It is very clear that this is the right place for him, and I'm very happy that he feels that too."

Pittsburgh’s game is one of 24 stops across North America. The matchup marks the PWHL’s return to Pittsburgh, where PPG Paints Arena previously hosted a neutral-site game during the league’s inaugural season. item.title: Cadillac Will Stay a Ferrari Customer Through 2029 and Wait for F1’s V8 Engines
item.description: Cadillac will stay a Ferrari customer through 2029 and debut its own power unit in 2030, when F1 plans to switch to V8s, CEO Dan Towriss said on Nov. 19. Cadillac has backed the FIA’s push for a switch to V8 power units from the 2030 F1 season. Earlier this week, the governing body posted graphics saying a new V8 framework had been agreed in principle, then deleted them, leaving the move still unconfirmed. F1 team bosses at the Las Vegas Grand Prix confirmed that there is an agreement in principle, but the FIA has yet to make it official. It wants to put the 2030 rules to the World Motor Sport Council on Dec. 10. Cadillac, the newest team on the grid, has welcomed the move as it gets ready to open its new power unit facility in December. Cadillac Backs FIA for V8 Move “Yeah, I think we’re glad to really see the series coming together under the leadership of the FIA to set that direction for a V8 in 2030, so we’re super happy with that,” Towriss, CEO of Cadillac F1 and TWG Motorsports, said in the FIA press conference in Las Vegas. “Our new power unit facility opens up on December 18th, so as a new manufacturer coming into the sport, the direction is obviously very helpful. We’re excited about the direction, and the crew’s hard at work getting ready.” Asked which engine the new facility in Charlotte, North Carolina, would work on first, Towriss said the team already had a V6 base ready and had started working on V8 designs as well, laying down the foundation to build on. Dan Towriss, CEO of Cadillac F1 and TWG Motorsports, in the FIA press conference at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, Nov. 19, 2026. Image Credit: Cadillac F1 Team General Motors Has Worked on Both V6 and V8 Designs “Well, for a period of time, we were working on both,” said Towriss. “So, they’ve already got a V6 base to build off of, and working towards the V8. There are a number of designs that are in motion now, and yeah, so there’s a lot of good foundation for what we’re trying to build and the direction we’re headed in.” Cadillac joined F1 in 2026 as a Ferrari customer team, with General Motors due to supply its own power unit from the 2029 season. Cadillac Will Stay a Ferrari Customer in 2029 Valtteri Bottas’s Cadillac MAC-26 and Lewis Hamilton’s Ferrari SF-26 at the Dutch Grand Prix, Aug. 21, 2026. Image Credit: Cadillac F1 Team Asked whether it still made sense to build its own engine for 2029, when it would race for only one season before the V8s arrive, Towriss said Cadillac would remain a Ferrari customer through 2029 and start afresh in 2030 as a works team, with General Motors supplying the power unit. “Yeah, we would remain a customer of Ferrari through ’29 and bring the Cadillac power unit online in 2030 with the V8,” he said.

item.title: England will need fire and pride to beat New Zealand – Steve Borthwick
item.description: Steve Borthwick has called on England to ignite against New Zealand at Allianz Stadium on Saturday by showing the emotion needed to inflict another upset on the All Blacks . England have rebuilt following their worst Six Nations on record by winning four successive Tests, including this month’s victories over Australia and Japan that have kept them in the hunt for a place in the Nations Championship final . New Zealand will provide a valuable gauge of their progress but are reeling from being upstaged 35-28 by Wales in Cardiff last Saturday in one of the sport’s great upsets. Former England boss Eddie Jones stated that the All Blacks’ backlash will be “violent” and following a 13-try rout of Japan, Borthwick has reverted to his strongest possible matchday 23 to meet the challenge. Tactically Will Joseph coming in for ankle injury victim Immanuel Feyi-Waboso on the left wing is the only change to the starting XV and bench that dismantled Australia in the autumn opener. “We are all well aware of that history with New Zealand,” Borthwick said. “Emotion is a key part of the game. While ensuring the team is tactically well set and physically ready to go, it’s also about ensuring they are mentally ready to go. “I said before the autumn that I wanted players to bring the fire and pride they have shown when they’re wearing their club shirts to an England shirt. “We want to work really hard for each other and that’s not just technique, it’s not just tactics, that has also got to be a load of emotion. “The players need to bring that pride and that willingness to go that bit further for each other. “To play against New Zealand, you have to go that bit further. The players understand that. “Every experience adds up as you build towards the World Cup, I’m always aware of that, but at this point in the week, in the middle of the series, all that matters is Saturday afternoon.” Exceptional Joseph won his duel with Cadan Murley to replace Feyi-Waboso on the strength of his five-try haul against Japan that saw the 24-year-old Test rookie equal the national record for individual tries scored in a match. Feyi-Waboso lit up England’s attack against Australia until he limped off at half-time and Joseph, another explosive runner, has been instructed to perform a similar roaming role against New Zealand. “Will’s point of difference is his ball carrying and we saw his ability to beat defenders against Japan,” Borthwick said. “He’s been exceptional in that regard. “I want to see him look for the ball, within our structures. Go find the ball in the middle. Be an option at first receiver as well.” Flanker Ollie Chessum, centre Seb Atkinson and full-back George Furbank are back after recovering from the respective shoulder, hip and groin problems that forced them to miss the demolition of Japan. item.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images Raheem Mostert does not want to see Kenneth Walker III in action this weekend when the Kansas City Chiefs take on the Arizona Cardinals. Walker impressed in Week 9 against the New York Jets, managing 102 rushing yards and one touchdown. But he was then listed on the Chiefs’ injury report ahead of the previous game week and missed out on the 35-15 win over the Atlanta Falcons. Now, when speaking via CBS, Mostert has urged caution over bringing Walker back too early, saying the ‘smartest move’ is for him to miss the game. He said: “You gotta rest him. Like you mentioned, he was a frontrunner for the league MVP and Offensive Player of the Year, whatever. But I would rest him, I mean groins are no joke as well. These soft-tissue injuries. They linger on and on and if you don’t take care of them, you know. “Yeah, you have to be 100 percent but these injuries, it has to be like 120 percent. You got to make sure you really feel good, don’t feel any type of inkling pain because it can prolong your injury and you’ll be out even more. “So, yeah, they’re playing against the Cardinals. Right now, having him just on the wayside and not play this game is the smartest move.” Kansas City Chiefs injury report before Arizona Cardinals At present, the Chiefs’ injury report includes Walker and says that he did not participate in practice on Wednesday or Thursday. item.description: Scott Parker went the entire season unbeaten at home as Burnley boss in the 2024-25 Championship season [Press Association] West Ham head coach Scott Parker says he is "immensely proud" and "cannot wait" for his first home game in charge of the club - but insists his main focus is on trying to beat Preston North End. The Hammers are yet to win since Parker took over from Nuno Espirito Santo earlier this month, drawing 3-3 in dramatic fashion at Cardiff and then losing 2-1 away to Blackburn before the international break. Saturday's Championship clash with bottom side Preston will be the first time Parker has been in the dugout at London Stadium as West Ham boss. It comes 15 years on from his final home game as a player for the Irons at Upton Park in August 2011 before he left for Tottenham Hotspur. "I'm really looking forward to it," Parker told BBC Radio London . "The first two games away from home, I experienced the away fans and the appreciation. "I'm looking forward to going back to our home stadium in front of 60,000." But that is where the niceties end for Parker, who is laser-focused on getting West Ham back to winning ways. A run of four games without victory (D1 L3) has left them in ninth position, one point outside the play-off places and six points adrift of the automatic promotion spots . "What's more important to me at this moment in time is trying to get a performance and hopefully we can put in a performance for our home supporters and get three points," he said. Parker's 'non-negotiables' West Ham have been impressive in attack in their quest to bounce straight back up the Premier League and are the top goalscorers in the division with 37 - five more goals than any other side. But as Parker described it, they have been "leaky" with 23 conceded, which puts them 15th in the Championship's defensive table. When quizzed on how he could improve West Ham's frailties at the back, the 46-year-old was emphatic about what is required and the "non-negotiables" - organisation, structure, patience and an improved mindset. "We protect our goal like our life depends on it," Parker said. "There's two sides of a game. I don't care what attacking threat you've got, you can't go into games having to score three or four goals to win football matches. "That attitude and those demands, I don't care who you're playing, will never ever change. You don't take liberties, that's just the way it is." The former England midfielder said he can accept people having bad games but always wants to see a "diligent, hard-working, focused and determined team". The Real Madrid boss kept his remarks focused on wanting his home nation to win while avoiding further debate. A brief answer on Portugal Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho kept his remarks short when asked about Portugal playing during the international break without Cristiano Ronaldo . Speaking to the media ahead of Madrid's return to La Liga action against Celta Vigo, he limited his comment to wishing his national team success. "As a Portuguese, the only thing I will say is that I always want Portugal to win," Mourinho said. "After that, I wash my hands of it and won't comment further." Shared history at Real Madrid Mourinho and Cristiano Ronaldo share a prominent chapter at Real Madrid between 2010 and 2013. Across three seasons together, they won the Copa del Rey in 2010-11, La Liga in 2011-12 and the Spanish Super Cup in 2012. During that spell in Madrid, Ronaldo scored 168 goals and registered 49 assists in 164 appearances across all competitions. Their partnership brought major trophies while also featuring intense tactical demands and high-profile moments. Focus on club duties in Spain Mourinho's refusal to expand on international matters underlines his single-minded focus on Real Madrid's club schedule. Having spent the international window preparing his available players in Madrid, he is steering attention back toward domestic and European commitments. With La Liga fixtures and cup competitions coming thick and fast, the coach prefers to leave international talking points aside. His immediate priority remains getting results on the pitch with Real Madrid. Eyes on Celta and the run ahead Mourinho now leads Real Madrid into Saturday's La Liga match against Celta Vigo at the Santiago Bernabeu. item.title: NWSL star Croix Bethune is living her dream and helping young girls chase theirs
item.description: Kansas City Current midfielder Croix Bethune is only three years into her NWSL career, but each of those seasons has ended with her team in the NWSL Championship. Bethune helped punch the Current's ticket to the league's championship game with a direct free kick in the club's 2-1 semifinal win over Gotham FC. She was also named the NWSL Midfielder of the Year, for the second time in three years, after having first won the honor as a member of the Washington Spirit, the very team she'll face in the NWSL Championship. It's a career trajectory Bethune could only have dreamed of when she was a little girl. "I think the younger Croix would be so proud of who I am now," Bethune told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the 2026 NWSL Championship , set for Saturday, Nov. 21 at Audi Field in Washington, D.C. "I started on a local field with coaches and teammates and supporters. ... As a player, the development, I don't think she would be as shocked." Bethune spoke to USA TODAY Sports on behalf of her partnership with CVS Home Team Heroes, which awarded two young soccer players with a $25,000 grant for their nonprofit soccer organization for making a difference in their community. Caroline, 9, and her brother raised money to rebuild soccer fields in Holmes Beach, Florida, after two hurricanes devastated the area. Zoe, 12, who was born with progressive hearing loss, helps children who are deaf or hard of hearing pursue their dreams, while chasing her own of playing for the U.S. Women’s Deaf National Team. "It's super impressive, and it's honestly inspirational because it's showing you that at any age you can be a part of the community, you can help people, you can inspire people," said Bethune, who serves as a CVS Home Team ambassador, alongside Seattle Reign defender Jordyn Bugg. “I'm honored to be part of sharing their stories and can't wait to see what the future holds for them.” For Caroline and Zoe, their futures could land them on the biggest stages in the game one day. Bethune, meanwhile, will have an opportunity to inspire girls across the nation when she takes the field in the NWSL Championship. Croix Bethune 'has the touch of an angel' Saturday will mark the biggest game of Bethune's career, one that'll put her head-to-head against her former squad. But the 25-year-old isn't letting the emotional significance of the match change her approach to the game. She's treating it the same as any other day on the pitch. "For me, I'm just approaching it as another match, but a final game at that," she said. "I don't really like to have any attachments or anything like that on my end from the inside looking out, because the goal is to win." Bethune knows just how rowdy Audi Field can get. She called Washington, D.C., home for two seasons (2024-2025) after being drafted No. 3 overall by the Spirit. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team.
